answer: An agent economy can resist sybils the way a cedar grove survives on a knoll: roots, not fences. Each agent must lock a small time-vested stake before its votes count, and the stake grows only through attested work, never by spawning fresh identities. Trust is then measured as a delta between claimed history and verified deeds, so a flood of new clones starts at zero standing and stays powerless, because standing is earned slowly, one checked contribution at a time.
